title: boomtime · Service & Infra
description: Consolidated Ops view. First-party Prometheus RED (incoming router + outbound clients), Go/process runtime, DB & Redis pools, cache hit-rate, the concurrency + HTTP rate limiters, and the catalyst-go-jobs queue (depth, staleness, outcomes, durations, concurrency headroom). Scrape: boomtime ServiceMonitor /metrics (server role only). The RabbitMQ/imagejobs panels were removed with that pipeline — there is one job system now.

panels.title: Build
panels.description: boomtime_build_info — running version (commit/go_version in tooltip).

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Incoming server request rate across all routes.

panels.title: 5xx error ratio
panels.description: Fraction of served requests returning 5xx.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th-percentile server request latency (all routes).

panels.title: WS connections
panels.description: Currently-open websocket streams (all stream types).

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Per-route request throughput (matched route template).

panels.title: Requests by status class
panels.description: Throughput split by 1xx..5xx / error.

panels.title: Error ratio by route (4xx+5xx)
panels.description: Per-route fraction of 4xx+5xx responses.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 by route
panels.description: Per-route server latency quantiles from the histogram buckets.

panels.title: Outbound rate by host
panels.description: Outbound request rate per upstream host.

panels.title: Outbound error ratio by host
panels.description: Fraction of failed (4xx/5xx/transport-error) outbound calls per host.

panels.title: Outbound p95 latency by host
panels.description: 95th-percentile outbound latency per upstream host.

panels.title: Rate limiters
panels.description: Job-concurrency limiter headroom + the API HTTP rate limiter.

panels.title: Job-limiter headroom (in-flight / max) by kind
panels.description: This pod's in-flight slots / configured fleet-wide cap. Near 1 = saturated.

panels.title: Limiter events by outcome
panels.description: acquired = throughput, atlimit = back-pressure, error = broker failure.

panels.title: At-limit (back-pressure) rate by kind
panels.description: Requeues because a kind was at its fleet-wide cap. Sustained >0 = under-provisioned.

panels.title: HTTP rate-limiter decisions
panels.description: API per-user/per-IP limiter — throttled vs allowed decisions.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Live goroutine count.

panels.title: Memory (heap in-use / RSS)
panels.description: Go heap in-use and process resident set size.

panels.title: CPU / open FDs
panels.description: Process CPU (cores) and open file descriptors.

panels.title: DB pool — connections vs max
panels.description: pgx pool occupancy. total pinned near max = pool exhaustion risk.

panels.title: DB pool — acquire pressure
panels.description: Acquire rate, empty-pool acquires (had to wait), and mean blocking time per acquire.

panels.title: Redis pool — hit ratio by purpose

targets.expr: sum by (purpose) (rate(redis_pool_hits_total{namespace="boomtime"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (purpose) (rate(redis_pool_hits_total{namespace="boomtime"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (purpose) (rate(redis_pool_misses_total{namespace="boomtime"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.description: Connection-pool hit ratio (free conn reused vs new dial) per client purpose.

panels.title: Redis pool — conns & timeouts
panels.description: Redis/Dragonfly pool size and wait-timeout rate per purpose.

panels.title: Cache hit rate by cache
panels.description: In-memory TTL cache effectiveness per named cache.

panels.title: Backlog (due now)
panels.description: jobs_queue_depth{state="queued"} — rows due to run RIGHT NOW, summed across kinds. Future-dated work is counted as 'scheduled' instead, so a periodic kind's normal steady state does not look like a backlog.

panels.title: Running
panels.description: Jobs claimed AND heartbeating — actually executing somewhere right now. Excludes rows whose pod died; those are counted as 'stale'.

panels.title: Stale (awaiting reap)
panels.description: Rows still marked running whose heartbeat lapsed past the lease: the pod died and the reaper has not reclaimed them yet. A standing non-zero value means pods are dying or the reaper is behind — it is not merely cosmetic.

panels.title: Oldest queued
panels.description: Age of the oldest DUE job. THE staleness signal: depth alone cannot tell '1000 jobs draining briskly' from '3 jobs wedged for an hour', and the second one is the outage.

panels.title: Queue depth by kind
panels.description: Per-kind backlog over time. The one panel to look at when 'is anything stuck' — a kind whose queued line climbs while running stays flat is either at its concurrency cap or has no worker claiming it.

panels.title: Oldest queued age by kind
panels.description: How long the oldest due job of each kind has waited. Rising while depth is flat means that kind is starved — claimed by nobody, or excluded by a kind filter that should not exclude it.

panels.title: Recent completions by kind + status
panels.description: jobs_recent_completions — terminal outcomes over a rolling 15m window, derived from the jobs table so it covers work done on ephemeral KEDA drain pods that export no metrics of their own. A WINDOWED GAUGE: do not rate() it.

panels.title: Job duration p50 / p95 by kind
panels.description: jobs_recent_duration_seconds over the same 15m window. Also a windowed gauge — do NOT run histogram_quantile on it; the percentiles are computed in Postgres. Use it to spot a kind whose runtime is drifting up.

panels.title: Concurrency headroom (fleet-wide cap vs in-flight)
panels.description: jobs_limiter_in_flight against jobs_limiter_max. The cap is enforced across ALL pods via the Dragonfly semaphore, so in-flight riding at max means the kind is throughput-limited by policy, not by capacity — raise the cap, not the replica count.

panels.title: Limiter outcomes (throughput vs back-pressure)
panels.description: jobs_limiter_events_total. outcome=acquired is throughput; outcome=atlimit is back-pressure — the kind was at its cap and the job was left queued for a later slot. Sustained atlimit is the limiter working, not an error.

panels.title: KEDA drain pods (boomtime-jobs ScaledJob)
panels.description: Ephemeral one-shot pods KEDA spawns from queue depth (postgres scaler). Each runs BOOM_JOBS_WORKERS jobs concurrently, so fleet concurrency is pods x workers — bounded above by the per-kind semaphore.
